text:
incident-bot: Alert: Dedicated pool eu-west-1 has sustained p99 token latency > 3.5s for 5m, capacity throttle detected :warning:
ana (oncall): saw it, paging SREs. I'm on it. tagging @matt and @jing
matt (sre): joining — what's the top-level symptom? p95 vs p99?
ana (oncall): p95 ~ 900ms, p99 ~ 3.6s, error rate normal, streaming stalls reported by a few customers. Dashboards: queue depth spiked to 520 for model redwood-llama-13b-q4.
jing (runtime): noted autoscaler failed to add hotshot nodes for this pool for ~45s due to handshake timeouts with provisioner. Warmup time for new instances ~30s, so scaling didn't cover burst.
devon (support): we've got 2 customer tickets reporting choppy streaming and dropped partials. Both are high-visibility (payment flows). Customers complaining of 5-10s stalls.
sam (product): estimated customer-visible SLO breach window started ~11:12 UTC. Any immediate mitigation?
matt (sre): first step: throttle lower-priority queues and switch affected customers to reserved fallback pool if possible. Can we identify impacted routes?
olga (eng-ml): adding: model kv-cache miss rate jumped ~80% during the spike — cold KV path exacerbating per-token compute. That inflates inference time on newly provisioned instances.
jing (runtime): runbook step: manual scale up of dedicated pool + route remap. I'm kicking manual scale now (request sent). Also increasing per-node warmup parallelism flag (hotshot_warmup_parallel=2) to speed readiness.
nx-deploy-bot: manual scale request accepted, provisioning 8 nodes (gpu-a100x1) — ETA ~35s
matt (sre): while nodes spin we should lower concurrency on streaming handlers for >10s callers. ana can you trigger priority-queue policy for payments to keep their tokens through?
ana (oncall): routing policy applied: payments -> dedicated-fallback-eu (smaller but warmed). Lowered concurrency for non-payment routes by 50%. :white_check_mark:
devon (support): notified both customers we are mitigating and provided ETA ~2m. They're on standby for follow-up.
jing (runtime): quick check logs: autoscaler logs show handshake retries 3x, then backoff due to transient DNS timeouts to provisioner endpoint. Ops networking also saw brief control-plane latency spike (~120ms). I'll open a ticket for infra.
matt (sre): observed streaming tail router queue depth drop after routing change. p99 dropped to ~1.2s within 75s of mitigation. Good sign.
nana (oncall): customer 1 reports partials resumed, customer 2 still sees occasional stalls (every ~30s).
olga (eng-ml): looking at prompt lengths: this workload has large KV usage + long contexts, so new instances had inflated memory GC on startup which blocked streams for a few seconds. Suggest we set gradual warmup ramp for this model in the pool config.
jing (runtime): agreed. We'll patch the pool profile: warmup_prefetch_kv=true and set warmup_sequence=128 for large-context models. Plan to roll in next deploy window but can flip flag for this pool now (hotfix).
matt (sre): recommended follow-ups: 1) investigate control-plane DNS retries 2) autoscaler backoff tuning (reduce initial backoff) 3) add ephemeral pre-warm for bursty clients (pre-provision N hotshot instances for known heavy customers) 4) add metric: handshake_fail_rate.
sam (product): tracking product impact: mark SLO breach for eu-west-1 dedicated on 2024-06-12T11:12Z window. Need postmortem with customer impact summary.
devon (support): logging customer ticket ids in incident doc: #C-4231, #C-4232. Will follow up with customers once we have postmortem.
nx-deploy-bot: manual hotfix applied: warmup_prefetch_kv=true on pool eu-west-1 (immediate).
jing (runtime): hotfix flipped. Observability shows KV miss rate trending down and p99 stabilizing ~800-1200ms.
matt (sre): ok we have steady improvement. I'll keep monitoring for 30m. Ana, please coordinate handoff to next oncall in 20m and prepare a concise pager summary.
ana (oncall): copying summary for handoff: "eu-west-1 dedicated pool saturation + autoscaler handshake timeouts caused warmup gap; mitigation = manual scale + route remap + warmup_prefetch_kv hotfix; customer tickets affected: C-4231, C-4232; p99 peak 3.6s -> stabilized ~1s; follow-ups assigned to runtime and infra."
ana (oncall): handoff ETA 20m, leaving channel open for any regressions. :hand:
jing (runtime): follow-ups assigned in tickets: INFRA-1120 (DNS control-plane spikes), RUNTIME-785 (autoscaler backoff), RUNTIME-786 (pre-warm policy).
matt (sre): adding action: add alert suppression when manual-scale in progress to avoid noisy pages.
devon (support): will update customers once postmortem is ready.
sam (product): I'll include mitigation timeline + affected customers in SLO report.
olga (eng-ml): will prototype warmup profile for large-context models and test in staging tomorrow.
ana (oncall): closing loop: if no regressions in next 20m I'll mark this incident as mitigated and start postmortem draft.
matt (sre): noted. Thanks all. 
incident-bot: Incident state changed: mitigated -> monitoring.
